label: training-gym-r33-complete
context:
Training Gym R33 completed. All 4 exercises 10/10.

R33 RESULTS (all 10/10):
1. bellman-ford-001 (T6) - Bellman-Ford shortest path with negative weight handling and cycle detection. 6 tests.
2. huffman-001 (T5) - Huffman coding compression/decompression with tree building. 6 tests.
3. eventloop-001 (T7) - Cooperative event loop with timer heap and generator-based coroutines. 6 tests.
4. interval-001 (T6) - Interval Tree (augmented BST) for point and overlap queries. 6 tests.

KEY PATTERNS:
- Bellman-Ford: relax n-1 times, early stop if no update, detect cycle with one extra pass
- Huffman: min-heap merge, single-char edge case needs left-only child, decode via tree walk
- Event loop: timer heap + task list, advance current_time to next event, process timers before tasks
- Interval tree: BST by start, max_end augmentation prunes branches, half-open intervals [start, end)

DB: 206 exercises, 371 attempts, avg 9.86
decisions: Bellman-Ford: track only reachable vertices in dist dict to handle sparse graphs
Huffman single-char: create tree with left child only, code is '0'
Event loop: separate timer heap from task list, advance time to min of both
Interval tree: BST key=start, max_end pruning: if query.start >= node.max_end, skip subtree
next_steps: Design R34 exercises. Focus on: Floyd-Warshall, Suffix Array, B-Tree, or coroutine scheduler.
